activeQuestion.prompt: What did the Lantern Room keep from the old red-chair practice, and what did it change?
activeQuestion.promptZh: 燈房劇場沿用了紅椅子習慣的哪一部分，又改變了哪一部分？

options.text: It kept requiring visitors to wait in the hall, but replaced the director with volunteers who answer questions.
options.zh: 仍要求觀眾留在大廳等候，但改由志工回答問題。
options.whyZh: 使用紅椅子的管道不必留在大廳，志工只負責收紙條，不是回答問題。

options.text: It kept the chair’s connection with asking the director questions, but changed how visitors submit questions and when they may receive answers.
options.zh: 紅椅子仍與向導演提問有關，但觀眾提問的方式，以及可能收到回答的時間，都改變了。
options.whyZh: 以前紅椅子表示導演留在現場接受提問；現在紅椅子收的是書面問題，日後才可能獲得回答。

options.text: It kept the chair as a sign that the director was physically present, but moved all questions out of the hall.
options.zh: 紅椅子仍表示導演人在現場，只是把提問一律移到大廳外。
options.whyZh: 試辦中椅子全程是空的，而且仍有觀眾留在大廳提問。

options.text: It kept giving an immediate reply to every question, but invited the audience to write their questions instead of saying them.
options.zh: 仍立即回答每一個問題，但改請觀眾寫下問題，不必開口。
options.whyZh: 導演只會選出部分書面問題，日後才在通訊上回答；文章也沒說以前每個問題都能立刻獲得回答。

activeQuestion.explanationZh: 保留的是紅椅子和它讓觀眾向導演提問的功能。改變的是做法：以前導演坐在椅上，就表示願意當面接受提問；現在椅子沒人坐，卻是收紙條的地方，導演可能日後才回答。空椅子不表示不接受提問。
activeQuestion.evidence: Red chair: originally seated director available after reading; during trial written slips passed to director to select for later newsletter. Some live questions continued.

vocabulary.note: 此處指寫有簡短問題的小張紙。
說明主持人或講者活動後還會留場。

group.title: A later start at the Lantern Room
group.titleZh: 燈房劇場為什麼晚一點開演
group.passage:
The Lantern Room tries a later start
By Mina Park, for the North Quay community newsletter

At the Lantern Room's monthly play reading, the first scene used to start at eight sharp. The evening bus reached the stop outside at 7:58. Its passengers usually got into the hall just as the doors closed, but many missed the spoken introduction, which started before eight. Without it, they could still hear the first scene, but might not know who was speaking or why the story opened in the dark.

For last Friday's trial, the introduction began at 8:03. The first scene followed it. Staff kept the interval between the introduction and the first scene unchanged. The theatre had always advertised eight as the start of the reading, and the trial notice clearly announced the change. Watching the last of the bus passengers settle before the introduction, the stage manager said, “For once, we're late at exactly the right time.”

The trial also brought back an old piece of theatre furniture: a red chair. Years ago, when a guest director sat in it after a reading, the audience understood that the director was staying to take questions. Last Friday the chair sat by the exit, empty throughout; a sign asked audience members to place written questions on its seat. Anyone could leave a question without waiting in the hall. Volunteers collected the slips and passed them to the director, who will select some to answer in a later newsletter.

The theatre used to report just one number after each reading: how many questions the director answered aloud in the hall. Some visitors still stayed to ask questions on Friday; those answers were tallied as usual. The slips put on the chair were counted separately, whether or not one would eventually be answered. “Both counts are worth keeping,” said the stage manager, “but please don't add them together and call the result a larger audience.”
group.passageZh:
燈房劇場試行延後開演
Mina Park 為《北碼頭社區通訊》撰稿

燈房劇場每月辦一次劇本朗讀會，過去一向晚上八點整開始第一場。晚班公車七點五十八分抵達劇場外的站牌。乘客通常在門快關上時才進入大廳，許多人因而錯過八點前就已開始的口頭導讀。他們雖然還能聽到第一場，卻可能不知道是誰在說話，也不明白故事為什麼在一片黑暗中開始。

上週五試辦時，導讀在晚上八點零三分開始，接著才是第一場。工作人員維持導讀與第一場之間的時間間隔。劇場以往一向公告晚上八點開始朗讀，這次也在試辦通知上明白公布調整。舞台監督看見最後幾位搭公車來的觀眾在導讀前就坐，說：「難得有一次，我們晚得正是時候。」

試辦也重新用上劇場的一件老家具：一張紅椅子。以前，如果受邀導演在朗讀會後坐在這張椅子上，觀眾就知道導演會留在現場回答問題。上週五，椅子擺在出口旁，全程沒有坐人；旁邊的告示請觀眾把寫好的問題放在椅面上。不必留在大廳等候，任何人都可以留問題。志工收好紙條交給導演，由導演選出幾個問題，在之後的社區通訊上回答。

劇場以前每場朗讀會後只公布一個數字：導演在大廳當面回答了幾個問題。上週五仍有一些觀眾留下來提問，那些當場回答的問題照常計數。紅椅子上的紙條另外計數，不論日後是否會獲得回答。舞台監督說：「兩個數字都值得保留，但請別把它們加起來，就說觀眾變多了。」

originalQuestion.prompt: What should a resident do to dispose of an old sofa?
originalQuestion.promptZh: 住戶若要丟棄舊沙發，應怎麼做？

options.text: Put it on the cardboard shelf
options.whyZh: 紙箱架供壓平紙箱使用，不收家具。

options.text: Leave it in the recycling room at any time
options.whyZh: 公告明確禁止把家具留在回收室。

options.text: Ask the morning cleaner to carry it away
options.whyZh: 公告提供的處理方式是預約清運，不是交給日常清潔人員。

options.text: Book a bulky-waste pickup with management
options.zh: 向管理室預約大型廢棄物清運
options.whyZh: 沙發屬家具，須預約大型清運。

originalQuestion.explanationZh: 沙發屬家具，須預約大型清運。
originalQuestion.evidence: These items require a bulky-waste collection appointment with the management office.

vocabulary.note: 讓紙箱變平以減少占用空間。
家具等體積大、需另外處理的物品。
